Slang 2026.21 folds uint64 comparisons with bit 63 set as signed values. The pinned slang-ir-sccp.cpp evalBinaryImpl dispatches comparisons using their boolean result type and signed intVal operands; slang-ast-val.cpp also uses signed comparisons. Rust preserves unsigned operand types and verifies the resulting words separately. These five divergent words are checked explicitly; shader execution parity is not claimed.

The pinned constant evaluators compare high-bit unsigned values as signed i64 because comparison dispatch uses the Boolean result type. Native evaluation preserves unsigned operands. Each compiled artifact must match its separate exact golden; full constant-folding parity remains incomplete.

Slang 2026.21 omits pointer-integer field sizes and offsets in JSON reflection. Pinned GetScalarLayout uses the target pointer size (eight bytes for HLSL). Both emitted buffers are independently checked against the same 120-byte DXC layout; native reflection is additionally checked by the native fixture.

Pinned DefaultLayoutRulesImpl reports half as two bytes, and Slang 2026.21 JSON reflection preserves that size. HLSL half occupies four bytes without DXC native 16-bit types. Native reflection describes that physical HLSL storage. Both reflection layouts and both 60-byte physical buffers must match separate exact goldens; complete source/target reflection parity remains incomplete.

Both exact physical extents and the matching source reflection are checked.
